description: Curated narrative clues for Cross the Impossible. Episode facts and result cards are joined from episodes.json at runtime.

entries.clue: A world-bearing creature imagined with a vast inhabited disc supported upon its shell.
A legend rooted in a gilded ruler and ceremonial offerings cast into Lake Guatavita.
Odin's immense hall, where warriors chosen after death gather beneath a shield-covered roof.
Fifty condemned sisters must endlessly carry water in perforated vessels that can never be filled.
The cattle yards that Heracles cleans in a single day by diverting river water through them.
The miraculous horn of plenty associated with an inexhaustible abundance of food.
The divine smith whose forge creates extraordinary arms and armour for gods and heroes.
The vessel whose identity becomes a paradox after every original component is gradually replaced.
Odin's spear, renowned for being unerring when directed at its target.
Odin's extraordinary eight-legged mount in Norse mythology.
A temporary winter residence assembled from frozen blocks and destined to melt after use.
A mythical bird consumed by fire before beginning another cycle of rebirth.
The legendary ram hide sought by Jason and the Argonauts.
The alchemical substance believed capable of transmuting base metals into gold.
Legendary footwear whose wearer can cover seven leagues in a single stride.
The many-headed monster of Lerna whose severed heads could regenerate.
Their guarded orchard contains Hera's golden apples, associated with immortality.
A reindeer-drawn flying vehicle used for a global Christmas Eve delivery mission.
The walking forest cabin of Slavic folklore, supported on articulated legs.
Winged footwear worn by the messenger god of Greek mythology.
The sealed vessel entrusted to a woman whose opening changes the human world.
The rainbow bridge connecting the realm of the gods with the human world.
The ship commanded by Jason on his voyage to retrieve a celebrated golden ram hide.
The immense world tree connecting the realms of Norse cosmology.
Odin's golden arm-ring, which produces eight equal rings every ninth night.
Captain Nemo's electric submarine in Jules Verne's undersea adventure.
The king whose granted wish causes everything he touches to become gold.
The young flyer who escapes Crete using feather-and-wax wings built by his father.
The condemned king who eternally pushes a stone uphill only for it to roll back.
The bronze guardian who circles Crete and attacks hostile arrivals with rocks and heated metal.
Thor's short-handled hammer, which returns to his hand after being thrown.
Daedalus' maze-like prison built to contain the Minotaur and defeat unaided escape.
Plato's island capital of concentric land and water rings, linked to the sea by a canal.
The hollow wooden offering used to conceal armed warriors inside the walls of Troy.
Arthur's sword of sovereignty and victory, associated with the mysterious Lady of the Lake.
The biblical tower whose construction ends with the confusion of human language.
The legendary cursed ship condemned to sail without ever reaching port.
The gold-plated vehicle driven by the sun god across the sky each day.
The legendary astral weapon described as possessing overwhelming destructive power.
The winged horse of Greek myth, associated with heroic journeys through the sky.
A time machine disguised as a British police box, with an interior beyond its external dimensions.
The stainless-steel sports car modified by Doc Brown for journeys through time.
A modified Corellian light freighter used on some of the galaxy's most famous missions.
A giant piloted defender that combines with the Spazer craft before launching from an underground base.
